observed_behavior: An actual Desktop worker executed exact frozen instructions, but acknowledgement failed because its native turn had no userMessage item.
expected_behavior: Acknowledgement recognizes the actual canonical delivery record and binds the original dispatch to its exact instruction turn without resend.
causal_mechanism: The fixture modeled private turn/start user inputs. The Desktop send tool instead inserts a functionCallOutput from codex_app/send_message_to_thread with a delegation envelope and once-escaped input. The generic parser discarded that output, making the acknowledgement input set empty.

anti_pattern.structural_description: A shared acknowledgement assumes the serialization of one transport also represents another independently owned execution transport.
anti_pattern.why_it_fails: The correct original instruction is present under another native item variant; ignoring its envelope rejects a real successful dispatch.

correct_pattern.required_invariant: Only the exact delivery representation of the selected native transport may establish receipt of immutable instructions.
correct_pattern.implementation_description: Preserve only the canonical Desktop tool output and require one strict UUID-source delegation envelope whose input equals canonical once-escaping of the frozen prompt. Direct user inputs still require exact byte equality; all original identity, generation and latest-turn checks remain.

applicability_conditions: A Desktop cross-session tool delivers prepared instructions to an original native worker
The actual turn stores delegation as a function-call output
known_non_matches: Direct private native dispatch stores a userMessage input
Unrelated tool outputs do not qualify as instruction delivery
confirmation_evidence: The exact original OBL-7 turn contained functionCallOutput, namespace codex_app and name send_message_to_thread, without userMessage
The raw envelope differed only by once-escaping &, < and >; canonical unescaping produced the exact frozen prompt
The corrected PostgreSQL provisioning Arc accepts the canonical escaped envelope
regression_proofs: tests/rolling-campaign-store.integration.test.ts: worker provisioning fences creation and atomically attaches the native identity and ignored marker
